10 year old critical vulnerability in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users across thousands of forums

Aikido
2026-06-10 5 use cases 2 techniques 4 kill-chain phases detected

Aikido Security discovered a critical unauthenticated authentication bypass in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users. A single HTTP request is all it takes to take over any account — a vulnerability that's been sitting in the codebase since 2014. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

phpBB Legacy OAuth Endpoint Exploitation Hunt (CVE-2026-29199) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts HTTP traffic to the pre-3.3.17 phpBB OAuth handlers (ucp.php?mode=login&login=external and ucp.php?i=ucp_auth_link&mode=auth_link&link=1) which are the surface for the unauthenticated session-takeover bypass disclosed by Aikido. After patching, the handler moves to /user/oauth/authenticate/ — sustained traffic to the legacy paths from a single source or with anomalous parameter shapes is either an unpatched instance under exploitation or a scanner probing the bug. Rationale: Anchored on the exact pre-3.3.17 OAuth handler URI patterns (`ucp.php?mode=login&login=external&oauth_service=...` and `ucp.php?i=ucp_auth_link&mode=auth_link&link=1`) — derivable from the article's stated patched path `/user/oauth/authenticate/...` and confirmed in the phpBB 3.3.17 release thread. These are the documented vulnerable endpoints rather than a generic phpBB login pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7gm6-w7mx-58cr
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate OAuth login flow on phpBB instances still running 3.3.16 or earlier — users redirecting through Google/Facebook/Microsoft hit the legacy path normally
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Nuclei templates) actively probing for CVE-2026-29199 from approved scanning IPs
  • Search-engine crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot) indexing the public forum login page
  • Internal pentest team replaying the PoC against staging copies of the forum
  • Bookmarked OAuth-return URLs from before the upgrade — long-tail user traffic for ~30 days post-patch
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("<approved-scanner-ip-1>", "<approved-scanner-ip-2>") and not (HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("Googlebot", "Bingbot", "AhrefsBot", "SemrushBot"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pivot on Src IP. Confirm the phpBB instance version (curl /styles/prosilver/theme/stylesheet.css HEAD, or check ACP). If ≥3.3.17, traffic to legacy path is suspicious; if ≤3.3.16, you have an unpatched forum that needs emergency patching. Pull the request body, User-Agent, and any session cookies issued in the response chain. Step 2 — Contain: If the instance is unpatched and the source IP is non-corporate, block the Src IP at WAF and force-expire all phpBB sessions (truncate phpbb_sessions table or restart php-fpm). Patch to 3.3.17 immediately. Step 3 — Hunt: Search for follow-on admin actions (ACP login, board configuration changes, attachment uploads, user permission changes) from sessions originating from the suspect IP in the next 24h. Cross-reference with UC2 (web-server-spawns-shell) on the phpBB host.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has "ucp.php"
| where Url has "mode=login" and Url has "login=external"
   or  Url has "ucp_auth_link" and Url has "mode=auth_link"
| where HttpStatusCode in (200, 301, 302, 303)
| summarize RequestCount = count(),
            DistinctUrls = dcount(Url),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            UserAgents = make_set(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, 5),
            SampleUrl = any(Url)
          by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname
| where RequestCount > 10
| order by RequestCount desc
title: phpBB Legacy OAuth Endpoint Access (CVE-2026-29199)
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-9abc-def012345601
description: Detects HTTP requests to the pre-3.3.17 phpBB OAuth handlers that the authentication-bypass vulnerability targets. After the fix, the OAuth handler moves to /user/oauth/authenticate/ so legacy-path traffic on a patched instance indicates probing.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce
  - https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1078
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.credential_access
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  uri_stem:
    cs-uri-stem|contains: 'ucp.php'
  oauth_login:
    cs-uri-query|contains: 'mode=login&login=external&oauth_service='
  oauth_link:
    cs-uri-query|contains: 'ucp_auth_link&mode=auth_link&link=1&oauth_service='
  condition: uri_stem and (oauth_login or oauth_link)
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate user OAuth logins on unpatched 3.3.16 instances
  - Vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Nuclei) probing CVE-2026-29199
  - Search-engine crawlers indexing login URLs
level: medium
source:(nginx OR apache OR cloudflare OR akamai) @http.url:*ucp.php* (@http.url:*login\=external* OR @http.url:*ucp_auth_link*) @http.status_code:(200 OR 301 OR 302 OR 303)
# log group: aws-waf-logs-<acl-name>
fields @timestamp, httpRequest.clientIp, httpRequest.uri, httpRequest.args, action, httpRequest.country
| filter httpRequest.uri like /ucp\.php/
      and (httpRequest.args like /mode=login&login=external/
           or httpRequest.args like /ucp_auth_link&mode=auth_link/)
| stats count() as requests, count_distinct(httpRequest.uri) as unique_uris by httpRequest.clientIp
| sort requests desc
| limit 100
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count, values(Web.url) as urls, values(Web.status) as statuses, values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents, dc(Web.url) as distinct_urls, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*ucp.php*mode=login*login=external*" OR Web.url="*ucp.php*ucp_auth_link*mode=auth_link*link=1*") by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.http_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count > 10 | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Web.url) as urls, values(Web.status) as statuses, values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents, dc(Web.url) as distinct_urls, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*ucp.php*mode=login*login=external*" OR Web.url="*ucp.php*ucp_auth_link*mode=auth_link*link=1*") by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.http_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count > 10 | sort - count
Web Server Process Spawning Shell — phpBB Post-Exploit RCE AIExploitation High
Detects apache/nginx/php-fpm spawning shell interpreters or download tools on a phpBB-hosting Linux server — the textbook follow-on to admin-level access via the CVE-2026-29199 bypass, which the article notes 'opens the door to Remote Code Execution' on phpBB 3.3.16/4.0.0-a2. Web servers should never legitimately fork /bin/sh or python in a phpBB context. Rationale: Direct response to the article's claim that admin access on 3.3.16 'opens the door to Remote Code Execution'. The parent-binary list maps to phpBB's documented hosting requirements (PHP via php-fpm or php-cgi, fronted by apache/nginx). The web-user account filter (`www-data`/`apache`/`nginx`/`_www`) is the privilege drop those servers do — this is the exact UID a phpBB RCE payload runs under. Cross-checked against: • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • phpBB attachment-handling code legitimately calling ImageMagick / ghostscript via PHP shell_exec for thumbnail generation
  • Cron-launched wrapper scripts (logrotate, awstats parsing apache logs) inheriting www-data when /etc/cron.d entries run as that user
  • Backup tools (rsnapshot, borgmatic) invoked under the web user during maintenance windows
  • Container entrypoint scripts where PID 1 is nginx/apache and the entrypoint forks /bin/sh
  • Custom phpBB extensions/MODs that legitimately shell out — e.g. video transcoder addons calling ffmpeg via /bin/sh -c
Suppression filter
| where ChildCmd !has "/usr/bin/convert" and ChildCmd !has "/usr/bin/identify" and ChildCmd !has "/usr/bin/ffmpeg" and not (ChildCmd has "logrotate" and ParentImage endswith "/cron")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pull full process tree (InitiatingProcessParentId chain) plus the ChildCmd. Look for tell-tale strings: curl/wget to attacker-controlled hosts, base64-decoded payloads, `bash -i`, `/dev/tcp/`, `python -c 'import socket'`. Inspect the phpBB host's recent access.log for the originating HTTP request (correlate by timestamp ±5s). Step 2 — Contain: Isolate the phpBB host from network (block all egress except patch-server). Kill the spawned shell PID. Pull memory image of php-fpm worker for forensics. Reset all phpBB admin credentials in the DB (phpbb_users.user_password) and force session truncation. Step 3 — Hunt: Run UC3 (web shell drop) over the past 30 days on this host. Search for outbound connections from www-data to non-RFC1918 destinations in DeviceNetworkEvents. Check /var/www/, /tmp/, /dev/shm/ for new files. Audit the phpBB ACP audit log (phpbb_log table) for admin actions in the suspect window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php-fpm", "php-fpm7.4", "php-fpm8.0", "php-fpm8.1", "php-fpm8.2", "php-cgi")
| where FileName in~ ("sh", "bash", "dash", "zsh", "ksh", "perl", "python", "python3", "nc", "ncat", "socat", "curl", "wget")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "httpd", "_www", "daemon")
   or  InitiatingProcessFileName has "php-fpm"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php-fpm", "php-cgi")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh", "/bash", "/dash", "/zsh", "/ksh", "/perl", "/python", "/python3", "/nc", "/ncat", "/socat", "/curl", "/wget")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "httpd", "_www", "daemon")
   or  ParentProcessName has "php-fpm"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Web Server Process Spawning Shell Interpreter (phpBB RCE Indicator)
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-9abc-def012345602
description: Detects apache/nginx/php-fpm/php-cgi spawning a shell interpreter or download tool, the canonical post-exploit pattern for the phpBB CVE-2026-29199 admin-account-takeover → RCE chain.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce
  - https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.execution
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/apache2'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/nginx'
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php-fpm7.4'
      - '/php-fpm8.0'
      - '/php-fpm8.1'
      - '/php-fpm8.2'
      - '/php-cgi'
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/ksh'
      - '/perl'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/socat'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
  condition: parent and child
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate phpBB image-processing modules invoking ImageMagick via shell_exec
  - Backup or cron-triggered cleanup scripts launched by web user
  - Container entrypoint scripts spawning shells under web-server PID 1
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @user.name:(www-data OR apache OR nginx OR _www OR httpd OR daemon) @process.executable.path:(*/bash OR */sh OR */dash OR */zsh OR */perl OR */python OR */python3 OR */nc OR */ncat OR */socat OR */curl OR */wget)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
ParentBaseFileName=/^(apache2|httpd|nginx|php-fpm|php-fpm\d+(\.\d+)?|php-cgi)$/i
ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|zsh|ksh|perl|python|python3|nc|ncat|socat|curl|wget)$/i
| UserName=/(www-data|apache|nginx|httpd|_www|daemon)/i OR ParentBaseFileName=/php-fpm/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count, values(Processes.process) as process_cmds, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php-fpm", "php-fpm7.4", "php-fpm8.0", "php-fpm8.1", "php-fpm8.2", "php-cgi") AND Processes.process_name IN ("sh", "bash", "dash", "zsh", "ksh", "perl", "python", "python3", "nc", "ncat", "curl", "wget", "socat") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user IN ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "httpd", "_www", "daemon") OR parent_process_name="php-fpm" | sort - first_seen
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Processes.process) as process_cmds, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php-fpm", "php-fpm7.4", "php-fpm8.0", "php-fpm8.1", "php-fpm8.2", "php-cgi") AND Processes.process_name IN ("sh", "bash", "dash", "zsh", "ksh", "perl", "python", "python3", "nc", "ncat", "curl", "wget", "socat") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user IN ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "httpd", "_www", "daemon") OR parent_process_name="php-fpm" | sort - first_seen
PHP Web Shell Dropped to phpBB Directory by Web Server User AIInstallation High
Detects creation of PHP-executable files (.php/.phar/.phtml/.php3/.php5/.phps) inside phpBB application directories by the web-server user — the persistence step after a CVE-2026-29199 admin takeover, since phpBB's ACP file-upload / styles / extensions features can be abused to plant a shell on the underlying filesystem. Aikido notes 3.3.16 admin access leads directly to RCE; the most common RCE technique is web-shell drop. Rationale: The article states 3.3.16 admin access 'opens the door to Remote Code Execution' — the phpBB attack surface for that includes ACP file uploads, style/template editing, and extension installation, all of which terminate in a file write under the web-server UID. Anchored to the canonical phpBB directory structure (`store/`, `cache/`, `files/`, `images/avatars/upload/`, `ext/`, `styles/`) and the PHP-executable extension family Apache will resolve. Cross-checked against: • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • phpBB version upgrade running install.php / phpBB/install/ writing migration PHP files into core directories — coincides with announced 3.3.17 rollout windows
  • Administrator installing a legitimate phpBB extension via ACP → writes new files into /ext/<vendor>/<package>/ under www-data
  • Style/theme installation writing PHP template helpers into /styles/<theme>/template/
  • phpBB cache regeneration writing data_*.php files into /cache/ on every cron tick or template change
  • composer install run under www-data for a phpBB extension dependency dropping vendor PHP files
Suppression filter
| where not (DroppedByCmd has "install.php" or DroppedByCmd has "composer install" or FolderPath has "/install/") and FileName !startswith "data_" and FileName !startswith "sql_"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pull the dropped file's SHA256 and content (cat from disk before it's wiped). Check against VirusTotal, look for `eval(`, `assert(`, `base64_decode`, `system(`, `passthru(`, `shell_exec`, `$_REQUEST[`, `$_POST[`, `<?php @`, `c99`, `r57`, `WSO` markers, or function-name obfuscation patterns. Compare timestamp to the phpBB ACP audit log (table phpbb_log) — was an admin logged in? Step 2 — Contain: Take the file offline (chmod 000, mv to /root/quarantine/), block source IP at WAF/perimeter, reset ALL phpBB admin passwords, truncate phpbb_sessions table, audit phpbb_users.user_type for unexpected founder/admin accounts. Take an EBS/disk snapshot of the host before further action. Step 3 — Hunt: Run UC2 (web-server → shell) against this host for the past 30 days. Search DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound connections from this host to non-corp destinations. Look for additional writes to /tmp/, /dev/shm/, ~/. Audit DB for unauthorised user_type=3 (admin/founder) rows. Check oth
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".php"
   or  FileName endswith ".phar"
   or  FileName endswith ".phtml"
   or  FileName endswith ".php3"
   or  FileName endswith ".php5"
   or  FileName endswith ".phps"
| where FolderPath has_any ("phpbb", "/forum/", "/ucp/", "/store/", "/cache/", "/files/", "/images/avatars/upload/", "/ext/", "/styles/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php-fpm", "php-fpm7.4", "php-fpm8.0", "php-fpm8.1", "php-fpm8.2", "php-cgi")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "httpd", "_www", "daemon")
   or  InitiatingProcessFileName has "php-fpm"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          FolderPath, FileName,
          DroppedBy = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          DroppedByAccount = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          DroppedByCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php", "phar", "phtml", "php3", "php5", "phps")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("phpbb", "/forum/", "/ucp/", "/store/", "/cache/", "/files/", "/images/avatars/upload/", "/ext/", "/styles/")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php-fpm", "php-cgi")
   and ActorUsername in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "httpd", "_www", "daemon")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileExtension,
          DroppedBy = ActingProcessName,
          ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP Web Shell File Written by Web Server Process in phpBB Directory
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-9abc-def012345603
description: Detects a PHP-executable file being written into a phpBB application or upload directory by the apache/nginx/php-fpm/php-cgi process — the persistence step in the CVE-2026-29199 admin-takeover-to-RCE chain.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce
  - https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/apache2'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/nginx'
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php-cgi'
  ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.php'
      - '.phar'
      - '.phtml'
      - '.php3'
      - '.php5'
      - '.phps'
  path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/phpbb'
      - '/forum/'
      - '/ucp/'
      - '/store/'
      - '/cache/'
      - '/files/'
      - '/images/avatars/upload/'
      - '/ext/'
      - '/styles/'
  condition: proc and ext and path
falsepositives:
  - phpBB upgrade scripts running install.php / database/migrations write phases
  - Legitimate ACP-driven phpBB extension installation by an authorised admin (correlate with ACP audit log)
  - phpBB cache regeneration in /cache/ writing data_*.php files
level: high
source:linux.auditd @user.name:(www-data OR apache OR nginx OR _www OR httpd OR daemon) (@file.path:*.php OR @file.path:*.phar OR @file.path:*.phtml OR @file.path:*.php3 OR @file.path:*.php5 OR @file.path:*.phps) (@file.path:*phpbb* OR @file.path:*\/forum\/* OR @file.path:*\/ucp\/* OR @file.path:*\/store\/* OR @file.path:*\/cache\/* OR @file.path:*\/files\/* OR @file.path:*\/images\/avatars\/upload\/* OR @file.path:*\/ext\/* OR @file.path:*\/styles\/*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
ContextImageFileName=/\/(apache2|httpd|nginx|php-fpm|php-cgi)$/i
TargetFileName=/\.(php|phar|phtml|php3|php5|phps)$/i
TargetFileName=/(phpbb|\/forum\/|\/ucp\/|\/store\/|\/cache\/|\/files\/|\/images\/avatars\/upload\/|\/ext\/|\/styles\/)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, UserName], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)
ENDPOINT

HTTP POST to pheditor.php with shell metacharacters in 'dir' parameter (CVE-2026-48030) AIDelivery High
Hunts for the CVE-2026-48030 exploit shape: an authenticated POST to pheditor.php with action=terminal and a dir parameter carrying shell metacharacters that bypass the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist. Targets the request layer (web/WAF logs) before any process or file telemetry fires. Rationale: Article PoC Step 4 explicitly demonstrates the exploit with `action=terminal` + `dir=/tmp; curl -s https://ifconfig.me #` — a literal semicolon in the dir POST parameter. We pin on the vulnerable endpoint string `pheditor.php`, the parameter shape `action=terminal` + `dir=`, and the shell metacharacters that bypass the whitelist guard the article quotes from lines 554–586. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin pasting a directory path containing a literal semicolon (rare but possible on Windows-style paths)
  • Security scanner (Nuclei, Nessus) probing pheditor.php with the published CVE PoC payload
  • Internal red-team or vulnerability validation exercises
  • Pheditor developers running PoC tests against a staging instance
Suppression filter
| where not (SourceIP in ("10.0.0.0/8", "<known_scanner_ranges>")) and not (RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus", "Nuclei", "Qualys", "Burp"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full POST body for the matching request — confirm action=terminal and the dir= value carries unescaped shell metacharacters. Cross-reference SourceIP against known admin/scanner ranges. 2) Contain: block SourceIP at the WAF/edge, force-rotate the affected pheditor admin password, and disable the terminal permission in pheditor config (TERMINAL_COMMANDS) until the host can be upgraded past v2.0.3. 3) Hunt: pivot on the web server host's DeviceProcessEvents for php-fpm/apache2 spawning shell/curl/wget in the next 5 min (UC2), and DeviceFileEvents for new .php files under /var/www (UC3).
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor in~ ("Imperva", "F5", "Cloudflare", "Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks", "ModSecurity")
| where RequestURL has "pheditor.php"
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestContext has_any ("action=terminal", "action%3Dterminal")
| where RequestContext matches regex @"(?i)dir=[^&]*(%3B|;|%7C|\||%26%26|&&|%24%28|\$\(|%60|`|%3E|>|%0A)"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, RequestContext, DeviceAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PHP/Apache web server spawning shell or LOLBin post-Pheditor exploitation AIExploitation High
Detects php-fpm, apache2, httpd, or nginx spawning interactive shells or network LOLBins — the immediate downstream signal of CVE-2026-48030 exploitation. The article's PoC Step 4 explicitly shows curl being executed via the dir injection bypass. Rationale: Article PoC Step 5 shows the attacker dropping a webshell via dir injection — the verbatim exploit chain is `dir=/var/www/html; echo '<?php system(...) ?>' > shell.php #`, and Step 4 shows curl being invoked. Both require the web-server user (article confirms `uid=33(www-data)`) spawning a child shell/LOLBin from php-fpm/apache. We pin on the parent (web server binary) + child (shell or download tool) + user (www-data and equivalents) triad. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Composer/Drush/WP-CLI maintenance scripts invoking curl from a CLI PHP context
  • Application cron jobs running under www-data that legitimately shell out
  • Container image build steps where Apache spawns curl during entrypoint
  • Site-health plugins (e.g. ManageWP) calling external endpoints via curl
  • PHP-FPM worker invoking ImageMagick/ffmpeg subprocesses for media processing
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/usr/local/bin/composer", "/usr/local/bin/drush", "/usr/local/bin/wp", "/etc/cron.")) and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--cron", "cli/php"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the child process's full command line — look for the article-specific patterns `ifconfig.me`, `> /var/www/*.php`, `<?php`, base64 blobs, or reverse-shell flags (`-e /bin/sh`, `bash -i`). Confirm the parent PID's TTY is null (web context). 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response, kill the parent php-fpm worker pool, snapshot /var/www for forensics, and rotate the pheditor admin credential. 3) Hunt: query DeviceFileEvents for new .php under /var/www on this host (UC3) and DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound from the same InitiatingProcessId (UC4). Pull the matching CommonSecurityLog row to identify the source IP that landed the exploit (UC1).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php")
| where FileName in~ ("sh", "bash", "dash", "ash", "zsh", "curl", "wget", "nc", "ncat", "python", "python3", "perl", "ruby", "socat")
| where AccountName in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "/php")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("/sh", "/bash", "/dash", "/ash", "/zsh", "/curl", "/wget", "/nc", "/ncat", "/python", "/perl", "/ruby", "/socat")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PHP webshell file dropped to webroot by web server process (Pheditor RCE) AIInstallation High
Detects new .php / .phtml / .phar files written under /var/www, /srv/www, or /usr/share/nginx by php-fpm, apache, or a shell spawned from them — the post-RCE persistence step the article shows verbatim in PoC Step 5. Rationale: Article PoC Step 5 literally executes `dir=/var/www/html; echo '<?php system($_GET["c"]);?>' > /var/www/html/shell.php #` and confirms RCE as `uid=33(www-data)`. We pin on the article's webroot path `/var/www/html`, the PHP file extension, and the web-server-user / web-server-process actor identity from the PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress/Drupal core/plugin auto-updates writing new PHP into wp-content or sites/all
  • Composer dependency installs into /var/www/vendor
  • Application caches that write PHP class maps (e.g. Symfony cache:warmup, Laravel route:cache)
  • Site backup-restore operations un-tarring PHP files
  • Pheditor itself being used legitimately by an admin to save a PHP file
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("/wp-content/upgrade/", "/vendor/composer/", "/var/cache/", "/storage/framework/cache/")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer install", "composer update", "wp core update", "drush updb"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: cat the new file — look for the article's signature payload `<?php system($_GET` or other one-liner shells (`assert(`, `eval(`, `passthru(`, `preg_replace(.../e)`). Capture SHA256 + file path. 2) Contain: quarantine the file (`chmod 000`), block its URL at the WAF, snapshot the host, then rotate the pheditor admin credential and disable the terminal action. 3) Hunt: pivot on the dropping process's PID to DeviceProcessEvents for other children (UC2), and to DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound the same PID made (UC4). Search all hosts for files with the same SHA256.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/var/www", "/srv/www", "/usr/share/nginx")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "sh", "bash", "dash")
   or InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/var/www", "/srv/www", "/usr/share/nginx")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php", "phtml", "phar")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "/sh", "/bash", "/dash")
   or ActorUsername in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Outbound C2 connection from PHP-FPM or Apache web server process (Pheditor post-exploitation) AICommand & Control Medium
Detects php-fpm, apache2, httpd, or nginx making outbound connections to public IPs — the C2/exfil signal that follows the article's PoC Step 4 (curl ifconfig.me) or a reverse shell from a dropped webshell. Rationale: Article PoC Step 4 explicitly fires `curl -s https://ifconfig.me` from within the web server context to confirm RCE — meaning the web-server PID makes an outbound connection. We pin on the web-server binary as the initiating process plus a non-RFC1918 destination, which is the article-specific shape (and unusual for a web server, which normally only listens, not connects outbound). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress site-health checks calling api.wordpress.org and other plugin update endpoints
  • Composer downloading dependencies from packagist.org (if PHP CLI runs as www-data)
  • License validation calls to vendor SaaS endpoints
  • Geo-IP enrichment plugins calling ip-api.com / ipinfo.io
  • Webmention/Pingback features hitting external blogs
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("wordpress.org", "packagist.org", "composer.org", "github.com", "github.io", "licensing.example.com")) and not (RemotePort == 443 and RemoteUrl endswith ".cdn.cloudflare.net")
Response runbook
1) Triage: enrich RemoteIP against threat intel; check WHOIS/ASN. Compare the timestamp against the web access log row for pheditor.php to see if the connection is within ~5s of the suspicious POST (UC1). 2) Contain: block the RemoteIP at the egress firewall, isolate the host if the connection matches known C2 infrastructure or is on a non-standard port. Snapshot the php-fpm worker's memory before killing. 3) Hunt: pull all DeviceNetworkEvents for the same InitiatingProcessId in the prior 24h, and check DeviceFileEvents for files written under /tmp or /var/www tied to that PID (UC3).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| summarize ConnCount = count(), Ports = make_set(RemotePort, 20), Urls = make_set(RemoteUrl, 20), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP
| where ConnCount >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SrcUsername in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| where DvcHostname has_any ("web", "app", "pheditor")
| where not (ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr))
| where isnotempty(DstIpAddr)
| extend Process = tostring(parse_json(EventOriginalUid))
| summarize ConnCount = count(), Ports = make_set(DstPortNumber, 20), Urls = make_set(Url, 20), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr
| order by FirstSeen desc

Repeated POSTs to pheditor.php with varying 'dir' parameter (discovery / whitelist probing) AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts for the pre-exploitation reconnaissance shape: a single source IP / session repeatedly POSTing to pheditor.php action=terminal with many distinct dir values, indicating an attacker probing path layout and whitelist boundaries before landing the CVE-2026-48030 exploit. Rationale: Article notes the exploit `completely bypassing the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist` — the attacker must first learn which paths/commands are interesting (PoC walks through /tmp and /var/www/html). The discovery shape is many distinct dir= values from a single source in a short window. We pin on the article's endpoint string `pheditor.php`, the parameter `action=terminal`, and high cardinality on the dir parameter. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1083 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin using Pheditor's file browser feature to traverse the filesystem
  • Automated configuration management touching pheditor.php for health checks
  • QA / regression test suites exercising the terminal endpoint with varying valid directories
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys) walking the endpoint with their CVE PoC fuzzer
Suppression filter
| where not (SourceIP in ("<admin_jumpbox_ips>")) and not (RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus", "Qualys", "PingdomTMS"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the dir_value samples — legitimate Pheditor use typically stays within app dirs (e.g. /var/www/html/<project>), while reconnaissance touches system paths (/etc, /bin, /usr/bin, /root, /home). Cross-reference SourceIP against the admin allowlist. 2) Contain: if SourceIP is non-admin, block at the WAF and disable terminal permission in pheditor config. Force-rotate the credential the session was using. 3) Hunt: pivot SourceIP forward in time for any POSTs that turned into successful UC2 process spawns or UC3 file drops, and backward for the initial authentication burst against pheditor_password.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "pheditor.php"
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestContext has_any ("action=terminal", "action%3Dterminal")
| extend dir_value = extract(@"(?i)dir=([^&\s\"]+)", 1, RequestContext)
| where isnotempty(dir_value)
| summarize DistinctDirs = dcount(dir_value), DirsSampled = make_set(dir_value, 20), Posts = count(), First = min(TimeGenerated), Last = max(TimeGenerated)
    by SourceIP, RequestClientApplication, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where DistinctDirs >= 5
| order by First desc
source:(nginx OR apache OR waf) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*pheditor.php* @http.request_body:*action\=terminal* @http.request_body:*dir\=*
WEB

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender

AWS CloudTrail StopLogging API invocation (logging disablement) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects invocation of the CloudTrail `StopLogging` API, which immediately halts log delivery from a trail to its S3 destination. The article identifies this as the most direct method to blind defenders; it requires only `cloudtrail:StopLogging` permission on the trail and typically precedes a larger attack. Rationale: Targets the article's explicitly named `cloudtrail:StopLogging` API (Technique 1). Filtering on `errorCode` absence ensures we catch only successful disablement; CallerType/CallerArn surface whether this came from a Root, IAMUser, or AssumedRole — Root or unexpected role identity is the high-fidelity pivot.
ATT&CKT1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised trail consolidation or migration to a new central account
  • Cost-optimisation deletion of duplicate trails by FinOps
  • IaC (Terraform/CloudFormation) tearing down ephemeral environment trails
  • Trail rotation as part of incident response evidence preservation
  • Account decommissioning closing out CloudTrail before account closure
Suppression filter
| where CallerArn !has_any ("role/TerraformExecutionRole", "role/CloudFormation", "AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole") and UserAgent !has_any ("cloudformation.amazonaws.com", "terraform")
Response runbook
1. Triage: identify the trail name from RequestParameters.name and confirm whether it is a primary security trail (multi-region/org trail) or a workload-specific one. Pull the caller's CallerArn and SourceIpAddress; check whether the call came from an approved IaC role/IP or an interactive session. 2. Contain: invoke `StartLogging` on the affected trail immediately; if the caller is unauthorised, revoke that principal's session tokens (`aws iam delete-access-key` / role session revocation policy) and rotate credentials. 3. Hunt: in the silent window (StopLogging → StartLogging) review GuardDuty findings, Config snapshots, VPC flow logs and any other parallel telemetry source for IAM privilege escalation, S3 data exfiltration, KMS key tampering, or new persistence (users, access keys, federation IdPs).
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where Application in ("Amazon Web Services", "AWS")
| where ActionType =~ "StopLogging"
   or (ActionType has "StopLogging" and ObjectType has_any ("Trail","CloudTrail"))
| extend RawData = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend TrailName = tostring(RawData.requestParameters.name),
         CallerType = tostring(RawData.userIdentity.type),
         CallerArn = tostring(RawData.userIdentity.arn),
         ErrorCode = tostring(RawData.errorCode)
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, CallerType, CallerArn, IPAddress, CountryCode, TrailName, ObjectName, UserAgent, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventName == "StopLogging"
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend TrailName = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).name)
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityType, UserIdentityUserName, UserIdentityArn, SourceIpAddress, AwsRegion, TrailName, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AWS S3 DeleteBucket targeting a CloudTrail log destination bucket AIActions on Objectives High
Detects deletion of an S3 bucket that is — or recently was — the destination for a CloudTrail trail. The article describes attackers with `s3:DeleteBucket` (plus `s3:DeleteObject` to empty it) destroying the long-term forensic store; after deletion the trail's configuration shows the bucket is gone. Rationale: The article calls out `s3:DeleteBucket` + `s3:DeleteObject` against the trail destination as Technique 2, with explicit screenshot of the trail showing the destination bucket missing. Naming-pattern heuristics for log buckets are the article-specific signal; pair with a known-good list of log buckets in your environment for the highest fidelity.
ATT&CKT1485 T1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Retention migration moving logs to a new bucket then deleting the old one
  • Account decommissioning during an org-wide consolidation
  • Terraform/CDK refactor that recreates the log bucket under a new name
  • FinOps cleanup of stale buckets after a workload sunset
  • Disaster-recovery test bucket cleanup
Suppression filter
| where CallerArn !has_any ("role/AWSControlTowerExecution", "role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole") and UserAgent !has_any ("cloudformation.amazonaws.com", "terraform", "control-tower")
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture BucketName, CallerArn, SourceIpAddress, UserAgent. Check whether the bucket was the active destination for any trail (`aws cloudtrail describe-trails` historical config) and whether a replacement bucket exists. Cross-reference with Config history. 2. Contain: revoke the caller's credentials/session if the action wasn't pre-approved, suspend the bucket-policy modification path, and check S3 versioning/object-lock to determine whether prior log objects can be recovered. 3. Hunt: timeline the window from last successful trail log delivery to bucket deletion; in that gap look at GuardDuty/VPC Flow/Config for IAM key creation, role assumption, exfil to public buckets, and any other Technique 1-5 indicators from the article.
let LogBucketHints = dynamic(["cloudtrail","audit","log-archive","-logs-","securitylogs","loggingbucket"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where Application in ("Amazon Web Services","AWS")
| where ActionType =~ "DeleteBucket"
| extend RawData = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend BucketName = tolower(tostring(RawData.requestParameters.bucketName)),
         CallerType = tostring(RawData.userIdentity.type),
         CallerArn = tostring(RawData.userIdentity.arn),
         ErrorCode = tostring(RawData.errorCode)
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| where BucketName has_any (LogBucketHints)
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, CallerType, CallerArn, IPAddress, CountryCode, BucketName, UserAgent
| order by Timestamp desc
let LogBucketHints = dynamic(["cloudtrail","audit","log-archive","-logs-","securitylogs","loggingbucket"]);
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventName == "DeleteBucket"
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend BucketName = tolower(tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).bucketName))
| where BucketName has_any (LogBucketHints)
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityType, UserIdentityArn, UserIdentityUserName, SourceIpAddress, AwsRegion, BucketName, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AWS CloudTrail DeleteTrail removing the trail configuration AIActions on Objectives High
Detects deletion of an entire CloudTrail trail via the `DeleteTrail` API — a step beyond StopLogging that destroys the trail's configuration including its S3/KMS/CloudWatch wiring. Unlike StopLogging this also removes evidence of how logging was originally configured, making restoration harder. Rationale: Reviewer-flagged: the article focuses on `StopLogging` but `DeleteTrail` is the related higher-impact API that removes the trail config altogether. Detection is a single-eventName match with success filter — extremely low FP; alert-worthy on any IAMUser/AssumedRole caller that isn't in a known IaC allowlist.
ATT&CKT1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IaC pipeline replacing a trail (DeleteTrail immediately followed by CreateTrail with same name)
  • Control Tower / Landing Zone account adoption renaming trails
  • Migration from individual-account trails to an org-wide trail
  • Retiring duplicate trails after central-trail rollout
  • Test account cleanup during sandbox tear-down
Suppression filter
| where CallerArn !has_any ("role/AWSControlTowerExecution", "role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole", "role/TerraformExecutionRole") and UserAgent !has_any ("cloudformation.amazonaws.com", "terraform", "control-tower")
Response runbook
1. Triage: was a replacement CreateTrail seen within ~5 minutes from the same caller? If yes and from an IaC role, likely benign rotation. If no replacement or a different caller, escalate. Capture CallerArn, SourceIpAddress, UserAgent. 2. Contain: re-create the trail with the prior configuration (pull from Config history if available) and re-enable logging; revoke caller's credentials if unauthorised. 3. Hunt: in the trail-blind window, pivot to alternative telemetry (Config, GuardDuty, VPC Flow, application logs, Defender for Cloud) for IAM persistence, KMS key changes, S3 data movement, federation-IdP creation, and any other Technique 1-5 indicators.

         CallerArn = tostring(RawData.userIdentity.arn),
         ErrorCode = tostring(RawData.errorCode)
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, CallerType, CallerArn, IPAddress, CountryCode, TrailName, UserAgent
| order by Timestamp desc
AWSCloudTrail

| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend TrailName = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).name)
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityType, UserIdentityUserName, UserIdentityArn, SourceIpAddress, AwsRegion, TrailName, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GCP Cloud Logging sink disabled via logging.sinks.update AIActions on Objectives High
Detects an attacker setting a Cloud Logging sink's `disabled` field to true via the `google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink` method — the GCP equivalent of CloudTrail StopLogging called out in the article. Once disabled, the sink stops routing matching log entries to their destination. Rationale: Targets the article's named GCP technique: `logging.sinks.update` permission used to set the sink's `disabled` field to true (Figure 1 in the article confirms the console message). Filter on `disabled:true` keeps this very low FP — most legitimate sink updates change filter expressions or destinations, not the disable flag.
ATT&CKT1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Planned cost-control pause of a high-volume sink
  • Sink destination migration where the old sink is disabled before deletion
  • SRE pausing a sink during BigQuery quota troubleshooting
  • Org Policy enforcement work that temporarily disables non-compliant sinks
  • Disaster recovery testing of sink failover
Suppression filter
| where Principal !has_any ("@cloudbuild", "@compute-system", "-terraform@", "@gcp-sa-") and Principal !endswith ".iam.gserviceaccount.com"
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull Principal, CallerIp, ProjectId, SinkName, SinkDestination. Identify whether the sink routes security-relevant logs (Admin Activity, Data Access, VPC Flow) or low-value app logs. Check change-management for an approved maintenance window. 2. Contain: re-enable the sink (`gcloud logging sinks update <name> --no-disabled`); if the principal is unauthorised revoke its session and audit recently granted IAM bindings for `logging.sinks.update`. 3. Hunt: during the blind window cross-reference VPC Flow, GCP IAM bindings, Cloud KMS key changes, and Workspace audit for IdP/role abuse; review whether other sinks in the project were also disabled or rerouted.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where Application in ("Google Cloud Platform","Google Cloud")
| where ActionType has "UpdateSink" or ActionType =~ "google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink"
| extend RawData = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend SinkName = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.request.sink.name),
         SinkDestination = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.request.sink.destination),
         Disabled = tobool(RawData.protoPayload.request.sink.disabled),
         Principal = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail),
         CallerIp = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp),
         ProjectId = tostring(RawData.resource.labels.project_id)
| where Disabled == true
| project Timestamp, Principal, CallerIp, ProjectId, SinkName, SinkDestination, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress
| order by Timestamp desc

GCP log bucket deletion via logging.buckets.delete (DELETE_REQUESTED) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the `google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket` call against a Cloud Logging log bucket. As the article notes, the bucket enters a 7-day DELETE_REQUESTED state before destruction, giving defenders a window to restore — but the deletion itself is the high-fidelity defense-evasion signal. Rationale: Article Technique 2 (GCP variant): `logging.buckets.delete` permission used to delete a log bucket; deletion enters DELETE_REQUESTED state for 7 days. The methodName is a fixed string so this is a deterministic single-event alert. Principal filtering catches unauthorised users vs known IaC service accounts.
ATT&CKT1485 T1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Decommissioning a stale log bucket after migration to a central project
  • Terraform destroy of an ephemeral project's logging infrastructure
  • Org-wide log retention rework consolidating buckets
  • Cleanup of test/sandbox project buckets
  • Cost-control deletion of an unused secondary log bucket
Suppression filter
| where Principal !has "-terraform@" and Principal !endswith "@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com" and CallerIp !in ("35.235.240.0/20")
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture Principal, CallerIp, ProjectId, BucketResource. Because GCP holds the bucket in DELETE_REQUESTED for 7 days, immediate restoration is possible via `gcloud logging buckets undelete`. Determine whether the deleted bucket held security-relevant logs. 2. Contain: issue the undelete within the 7-day window; revoke the principal's session and audit recently granted `logging.admin` / `logging.bucketsAdmin` bindings. 3. Hunt: pivot to other techniques described in the article — was a sink also disabled (UpdateSink), is a parallel attacker-owned export sink siphoning logs to an external project, has the KMS CMEK for the bucket been rotated or revoked?
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where Application in ("Google Cloud Platform","Google Cloud")
| where ActionType has "DeleteBucket" and ActionType has "logging"
   or ActionType =~ "google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket"
| extend RawData = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend BucketResource = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.resourceName),
         Principal = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail),
         CallerIp = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp),
         ProjectId = tostring(RawData.resource.labels.project_id),
         ErrorCode = tostring(RawData.protoPayload.status.code)
| where ErrorCode in ("","0")
| project Timestamp, Principal, CallerIp, ProjectId, BucketResource, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress
| order by Timestamp desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Inbound WebSocket upgrade to phoenix_storybook playground from external source
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] HEEx attribute breakout payload in psb-assign WebSocket message · [LLM] Erlang SASL CompileError / template compilation spike from BEAM · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-8467: PhoenixStorybook: Unauthenticated remote code e
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BEAM (beam.smp / erl) spawning shell or OS command — post-exploit code execution
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

Inbound WebSocket upgrade to phoenix_storybook playground from external source AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for HTTP(S) requests to phoenix_storybook playground URI paths (e.g. /storybook/*) carrying a WebSocket upgrade from non-RFC1918 source addresses. CVE-2026-8467 lets any unauthenticated WS client reach the vulnerable psb-assign handler, so any public hit on this path is suspicious unless the storybook is intentionally exposed. Rationale: Article specifies /storybook/<component> URL pattern and 'unauthenticated WebSocket' access — any public-IP hit on this path is the entry point for CVE-2026-8467. Cross-checked GitHub advisory GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p and the introduction commit e35379d on phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/56ab8464d4375fa52db806148a06cce126ad481d
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal developer reviewing the component catalogue from a VPN exit IP that NATs to a public address
  • CI/CD pipeline running Lighthouse/Playwright against staging that includes /storybook
  • Search-engine crawler indexing a misconfigured staging environment
  • Internal vuln-scanner (Tenable / Qualys) probing the storybook URL
  • Marketing/design team showing the storybook to an external partner over screen-share
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !has_any ("GoogleBot","Bingbot","Playwright","HeadlessChrome","Qualys","Nessus")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — confirm the destination host actually runs phoenix_storybook and check version (vulnerable: >=0.5.0 <1.1.0). Pivot the source IP across W3CIIS / WAF for repeated psb-assign WS frames. 2) CONTAIN — if exposure is unintentional, block the path at the WAF/reverse proxy and remove storybook from production routes; if intentional, upgrade phoenix_storybook to >=1.1.0 immediately. 3) HUNT — pivot the BEAM host across DeviceProcessEvents for beam.smp spawning sh/cmd/powershell and DeviceNetworkEvents for new outbound connections from the BEAM uid in the same time window.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlsrv.exe")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem startswith "/storybook" or csUriStem contains "phoenix_storybook"
| where csMethod =~ "GET"
| where not(ipv4_is_private(cIP))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus, sPort
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Inbound request to phoenix_storybook playground path
id: f4d7ce10-2a1c-4b34-9f4d-2d28a1a4d301
description: Detects HTTP GET requests to phoenix_storybook playground endpoints (CVE-2026-8467 attack surface).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p
author: detection-pipeline
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: GET
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/storybook/'
      - 'phoenix_storybook'
  condition: selection
level: medium
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:envoy) @http.method:GET (@http.url_details.path:*/storybook/* OR @http.url:*storybook*) -CIDR(@network.client.ip, 10.0.0.0/8) -CIDR(@network.client.ip, 172.16.0.0/12) -CIDR(@network.client.ip, 192.168.0.0/16)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ConnectionDirection=1
| ContextImageFileName=/(beam\.smp|erl\.exe|erlsrv\.exe)/i
| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4) AND NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4) AND NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, LocalPort], function=count())
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web where Web.url_path="*/storybook/*" Web.http_method="GET" by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_method, Web.http_user_agent, _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where NOT cidrmatch("10.0.0.0/8",src) AND NOT cidrmatch("172.16.0.0/12",src) AND NOT cidrmatch("192.168.0.0/16",src)
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.url_path="*/storybook/*" Web.http_method="GET" by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_method, Web.http_user_agent, _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where NOT cidrmatch("10.0.0.0/8",src) AND NOT cidrmatch("172.16.0.0/12",src) AND NOT cidrmatch("192.168.0.0/16",src)
HEEx attribute breakout payload in psb-assign WebSocket message AIExploitation High
Detects request bodies or URLs to phoenix_storybook playground that carry the article's specific HEEx attribute-breakout signature (literal '" injected={', '<%=', or dangerous Elixir Kernel calls like System.cmd / Code.eval / File.write / Port.open). Targets the CVE-2026-8467 exploitation payload directly. Rationale: Pulls the exact attribute-breakout signature the advisory shows ('foo" injected={EXPR} bar="') and the example dangerous call (System.cmd) plus other Kernel sinks (Code.eval, EEx.eval, File.write, Port.open) that an attacker would chain. The psb-assign event name is unique to PlaygroundPreviewLive, making it a strong anchor. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/e35379dfe2ef1a71b141899e36f431017c55265d
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher running an authorized PoC against the patched version
  • WAF vendor test traffic that probes for Elixir/Phoenix RCE signatures
  • Storybook documentation page legitimately referencing System.cmd as example text
  • Internal pentest replay of GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p against staging
  • Bug-bounty hunter scanning before formal disclosure
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<authorized_pentest_ip>","<bug_bounty_relay>"]))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — capture the full request URI/body; confirm phoenix_storybook version on the target host. If <1.1.0 and the payload contains a Kernel call, treat as confirmed exploitation. 2) CONTAIN — block source IP at the edge, isolate the BEAM host, snapshot for forensics; rotate any secrets accessible to the BEAM service account. 3) HUNT — pivot BEAM host process tree (beam.smp → sh/cmd) for the last 30 days, check outbound DNS/HTTP from BEAM uid, search Git/build artefacts for unexpected commits if the host had repo access.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlsrv.exe")
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("psb-assign","System.cmd","injected={","Code.eval","EEx.eval","<%=")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL contains "storybook" or DeviceCustomString1 contains "storybook"
| where RequestURL has_any ("psb-assign","System.cmd","injected={","Code.eval","EEx.eval","File.write","Port.open","<%=","%3C%25")
   or Message has_any ("psb-assign","System.cmd","injected={","Code.eval","<%=")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestMethod, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

BEAM (beam.smp / erl) spawning shell or OS command — post-exploit code execution AIInstallation High
Detects the Erlang BEAM runtime spawning shells or LOLBins, which should never happen in normal phoenix_storybook operation. CVE-2026-8467 lets attacker code run with full Kernel access, and System.cmd/Port.open is the canonical example — this query catches the resulting child process. Rationale: Article calls out 'full Elixir Kernel access' and System.cmd/2 as the PoC sink. BEAM has no legitimate reason to fork sh/cmd in a phoenix_storybook deployment — any such child is a near-deterministic RCE signal. Cross-checked with GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p patch commit 56ab8464 which adds attribute-value escaping. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/56ab8464d4375fa52db806148a06cce126ad481d
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1548
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom mix release using System.cmd to call git/uname for runtime version banners
  • Phoenix LiveDashboard or Telemetry plugin shelling out to read /proc on Linux
  • Erlang :os.cmd usage in a legitimate health-check endpoint
  • Mix tasks that wrap external compilers (e.g. SASS, esbuild) at runtime
  • Containerised BEAM image with an entrypoint script invoking erl as PID 1 then forking sidecars
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !contains "liveDashboard" and ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("git rev-parse","uname -a","hostname")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — fetch the child ProcessCommandLine; if it includes reverse-shell strings (sh -i, bash -c, curl|sh) treat as confirmed RCE. Correlate with the inbound WebSocket source IP from UC1. 2) CONTAIN — kill the child process, isolate the host from network, snapshot memory; rotate the BEAM service account creds, any secrets in app config, and any cloud credentials reachable from the host's IAM role. 3) HUNT — pivot the same parent across the fleet; look for AsepValueUpdate / cron / systemd unit writes from beam.smp in the last 30 days; check DNS for newly-resolved domains from this host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlsrv.exe","erl")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlsrv.exe","erl")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

BEAM Erlang distribution protocol (EPMD / port 4369) outbound from phoenix_storybook host AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the BEAM runtime initiating outbound TCP to EPMD (4369) or the Erlang distribution port range (4370-40000 typical) toward hosts not in the known cluster topology. Post-RCE via CVE-2026-8467, an attacker with full Kernel access can use :net_kernel.connect_node/1 to pivot to peer BEAM nodes. Rationale: BEAM RCE that grants Kernel access lets an attacker invoke :net_kernel.connect_node and pivot across the cluster. EPMD on 4369 plus the Erlang dist port range is the unique TCP fingerprint of that pivot — combined with beam.smp as the initiating process it's a high-value hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p
ATT&CKT1570 T1021
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Elixir cluster nodes joining via libcluster gossip
  • Kubernetes BEAM pods discovering peers via headless service DNS
  • Phoenix PubSub clustering after a rolling deploy
  • Observer / wx-tracing connection from a developer workstation
  • Distillery / Mix release hot-upgrade negotiating with the running node
Suppression filter
| where RemoteIP !in (dynamic(["<known_cluster_node_1>","<known_cluster_node_2>"]))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — confirm the RemoteIP is not in the known BEAM cluster inventory; if it is, suppress and move on. If unknown, correlate with UC1/UC2 hits on the same host in the prior 1h. 2) CONTAIN — block 4369 + the distribution port range egress from the storybook host at the host firewall; rotate the Erlang cookie (~/.erlang.cookie) and force re-clustering. 3) HUNT — query every other BEAM host in the fleet for inbound 4369 from the compromised IP, and for new node names visible via :erlang.nodes/0 or its log output.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlsrv.exe")
| where RemotePort == 4369 or (RemotePort between (4370 .. 40000))
| where RemoteIPType != "Loopback"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), HitCount=count() by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstPortNumber == 4369 or (DstPortNumber between (4370 .. 40000))
| where DvcHostname has_any ("beam","phoenix","storybook") or SrcHostname has_any ("beam","phoenix","storybook")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), HitCount=count() by SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| order by FirstSeen desc

Erlang SASL CompileError / template compilation spike from BEAM AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for bursts of Erlang/Elixir compilation or evaluation errors (CompileError, SyntaxError, TokenMissingError, ArgumentError around EEx/Code.eval) from the BEAM host serving phoenix_storybook. CVE-2026-8467 exploits inject HEEx that must compile; malformed probes will produce a distinctive error sequence even when the successful payload runs silently. Rationale: Article explicitly names EEx.compile_string/2, Code.eval_quoted_with_env/3, PlaygroundPreviewLive and ComponentRenderer.attributes_markup/1 — these strings appear in stack traces when an injection probe fails. A burst of CompileError/SyntaxError naming these modules is the cleanest signal short of full WS frame inspection. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/56ab8464d4375fa52db806148a06cce126ad481d
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1190
Data sourcesAlerts
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer hot-reloading templates locally producing CompileError bursts
  • CI test run failing template compilation against staging
  • Live coding session via IEx remote shell
  • Phoenix LiveReload triggering compile cycles after file save
  • Application boot-time compile errors after a bad deploy
Suppression filter
| where HostName !in (dynamic(["<dev_hostname_1>","<dev_hostname_2>","<ci_runner_hostname>"]))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — pull a sample stack trace; if it names PlaygroundPreviewLive or ComponentRenderer.attributes_markup correlating with external WebSocket traffic in UC1/UC2, treat as exploitation attempts. 2) CONTAIN — block source IP at the WAF, upgrade phoenix_storybook to >=1.1.0, optionally remove the playground route from production via config. 3) HUNT — for any host with the spike, check UC3 (BEAM child shells) and UC4 (4369 outbound) in the prior 1h; if either fires, treat as confirmed RCE and pivot to full IR.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog

| where ProcessName has_any ("beam.smp","erl","erlsrv") or SyslogMessage has_any ("PlaygroundPreviewLive","ComponentRenderer","EEx.compile_string")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("CompileError","SyntaxError","TokenMissingError","Code.eval_quoted_with_env","** (CompileError","** (SyntaxError")
| summarize ErrCount=count() by HostName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where ErrCount > 5
| order by TimeGenerated desc

June 2026 Patch Tuesday — exposure inventory for critical RCE CVEs AIWeaponization High
Hunts devices still missing the June 2026 Microsoft critical patches called out by Talos as 'more likely' exploited (Remote Desktop Client heap overflow, HTTP.sys integer overflow, Win32K GRFX, Kernel TCP/IP UAF) plus the other critical 'less likely' RCEs. Turns Patch Tuesday into an actionable exposure list so SOC and IT-Ops can chase the long tail before the public PoCs land. Rationale: Hard-codes the exact CVE list from the Talos blog (the four 'more likely' CVEs + the 23 'less likely' criticals). Joins to DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilitiesKB so devices with public PoCs bubble to the top. No external corroboration searched — Talos blog is itself a vendor write-up of MSRC.

| where DeviceName !has "-test" and DeviceName !has "-lab" and DeviceName !has "-image"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot the result into MEM/Intune or WSUS console — confirm whether each device's missing patch is queued, failed, or never offered. Cross-check internet exposure with DeviceInfo IsInternetFacing for any host carrying CVE-2026-47291 (HTTP.sys) or CVE-2026-44815 (DHCP). 2) Contain: isolate any internet-facing host missing 'more likely' CVEs until patched; for RDP-Client CVEs, push GPO blocking outbound 3389 to untrusted networks until mstsc is patched. 3) Hunt: pivot exposed hosts into UC2-UC5 to look for active exploitation evidence (mstsc child processes, w3wp children, vmwp anomalies, Outlook preview-pane spawns).
let JuneCriticalCVEs = dynamic(["CVE-2026-42985","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44803","CVE-2026-44812","CVE-2026-42992","CVE-2026-44799","CVE-2026-44801","CVE-2026-47289","CVE-2026-48563","CVE-2026-45607","CVE-2026-45641","CVE-2026-47652","CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-48574","CVE-2026-42987","CVE-2026-44815","CVE-2026-45456","CVE-2026-45458","CVE-2026-47635","CVE-2026-45461","CVE-2026-45463","CVE-2026-45472","CVE-2026-45474","CVE-2026-44810","CVE-2026-32193","CVE-2026-45648","CVE-2026-47644","CVE-2026-45476","CVE-2026-26142"]);
